relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.object: administrator use only - not accessible from clients directly
relations.evidence: The Admin REST API is for administrator use only, and hence is **not** accessible from the clients directly.

relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.evidence: To allow users to access the Admin API up you need to create a Couchbase Server-based RBAC-user for them — see: [REST API Access](rest-api-access.md).

notable_absence.finding: This page states in its own NOTE callout, unambiguously, exactly the mechanism round 27 inferred from elsewhere: for document changes sent through the Admin REST API, 'the Sync Function executes with admin privileges. Calls to requireUser, requireAccess and requireRole will be no-ops, and will always appear successful.' This is the single clearest first-party statement of that mechanism found so far in one place - most other pages state it per require*() command (each command's own reference page) rather than once, generally, at the API level.

cross_component_finding: This page is the strongest confirmation yet that Sync Gateway's Admin REST API sits at the seam between its two disjoint access-control systems: paragraph 2 sends the reader to create a 'Couchbase Server-based RBAC-user' (sgw:rbac-user, the reused Server RBAC system) merely to be ALLOWED to call the API at all, while the NOTE callout describes what that same API does to the OTHER system (sgw:user/channel/require*() checks) once a call is authenticated - collapsing both halves of the two-layer model onto one page for the first time.
cross_product_finding: The page links out to Couchbase Server's own RBAC role catalogue (../../../server/current/learn/security/roles.md) as the authority for 'RBAC role requirements' on Sync Gateway Admin REST API endpoints - confirming Sync Gateway does not define its own privilege catalogue for this surface at all, it borrows Server's whole-cloth (consistent with role:* concepts already in the registry from server/).
